key_insight: HEM-Med separates transferable cross-hospital prescribing experience from hospital-specific patterns, then uses safety-aware decoding to recommend medications more safely across multiple centers.
clinical_relevance: This could help smaller hospitals benefit from large-center learning while better respecting local formulary constraints and reducing unsafe drug combinations.
method: Builds a hierarchical memory of patient medication context
Disentangles memory into cross-hospital experience and hospital-specific residuals
Uses safety-aware set generation with dual-level retrieval for medication recommendation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on a real-world multi-center eICU dataset, where HEM-Med outperformed transfer learning, LLM-based, and other medication recommendation baselines on accuracy and safety.
watch_item: Performance is shown on one multi-center dataset, so broader validation is needed before assuming the same safety and generalization in other hospitals.
paper_title: HEM-Med: A Hierarchical Agentic Memory Framework for Safe Multi-Center Medication Recommendation
